title: Walk among the earth towers of Đavolja Varoš
description: 202 stone-capped earth pillars formed by erosion, with a spring beside them so acidic it corrodes metal. Local legend says the pillars are a wedding party turned to stone.

title: Cruise the Iron Gates gorge below Golubac fortress
description: Nine towers on the Danube where the river narrows into Europe's biggest gorge system. Boat trips run from the fortress into the gorge itself, since the best view of the walls is from the water.

title: Photograph the house on the Drina river
description: A one-room cabin built on a rock in the middle of the river in 1968 by swimmers who wanted somewhere to sunbathe away from the current. Rebuilt more than once after floods took it.

title: Watch griffon vultures over the Uvac meanders
description: Hairpin river bends carved through limestone, with one of the last griffon vulture colonies in the Balkans nesting on the cliffs. The viewpoint at Molitva is a short, steep walk from the car park.

title: Explore the Roman palace at Gamzigrad
description: Emperor Galerius built this palace to be deified in after death, and it stood barely used for that purpose for a century. Mosaic floors survive in situ, with almost no other visitors around them.

title: See the Skull Tower in Nis
description: A tower built from the skulls of Serbian rebels by the Ottomans in 1809 as a warning, now a chapel protecting the fifty-eight skulls that remain. It stops most visitors mid-sentence.

title: Dance at Exit Festival inside Petrovaradin fortress
description: Four nights of international lineups across stages built into the fortress casemates. Started in 2000 as a student protest against the Milosevic government and never stopped.

title: Stand where the Latin Bridge assassination started a world war
description: Franz Ferdinand's car took a wrong turn here in 1914 and Gavrilo Princip was waiting. A small museum on the corner covers the assassination in more depth than the plaque outside does.

title: Walk or ride a carriage at Vrelo Bosne
description: Dozens of springs feed the Bosna river out of the ground here in a park of poplar-lined channels and swans. Horse-drawn carriages run the tree-lined avenue from the tram stop.

title: Visit the dervish house under the Buna spring cliff
description: A 16th-century Sufi lodge built into the base of a 200-metre cliff, right where the Buna river erupts from a cave. One of the most powerful natural springs in Europe.

title: Drink coffee under the plane trees in Trebinje
description: An Ottoman-Mediterranean old town on the Trebisnjica river, an hour from Dubrovnik and a fraction of the crowd. The Arslanagic bridge and the hilltop Hercegovacka Gracanica church are both a short walk out.

title: See the waterfall in the middle of Jajce
description: A 21-metre drop where two rivers meet in the centre of town, overlooked by a medieval fortress where Bosnia's last king was crowned. The mist reaches the main square on a windy day.

title: Raft the Una at Strbacki buk
description: An emerald river split into channels by wooded islands, with a 24-metre cascade at Strbacki buk that rafts run right over. Far quieter than Plitvice across the border, for the same limestone-and-waterfall scenery.

title: Hike into the Perucica primeval forest
description: One of the last two primary forests left in Europe, with trees over 300 years old and a waterfall you view from a wooden platform because the reserve core is closed to walkers. The Skakavac viewpoint is the easiest way in.

title: Climb the fortified hill village of Pocitelj
description: A walled Ottoman village of stone houses and a citadel tower on the Neretva, badly damaged in the 1990s war and still being restored stone by stone. Fig and pomegranate stalls line the path up.

title: Take a boat to Our Lady of the Rocks
description: An artificial islet built up over centuries by sailors dropping stones on a reef after a vow, now a chapel crowded with votive paintings from grateful captains. Boats leave from Perast whenever a few passengers gather.

title: Walk the baroque waterfront of Perast
description: Seventeen baroque palaces built by sea-captain families along a single waterfront street, with none of Kotor's cruise-ship crowds. Climb St Nicholas' bell tower for the view down onto both islets.

title: Hike the loop around Black Lake
description: A glacial lake ringed by pines below Bobotov Kuk, Durmitor's highest peak. The easy path around it is crowded by midday in August; go for sunrise and it's just you and the reflections.

title: Visit the monastery built into the cliff at Ostrog
description: A working monastery carved into a vertical rock face 900 metres up, holding relics that draw pilgrims of every faith in the region. The upper monastery has no parking; most people walk up from the lower one.

title: Climb to the Njegos mausoleum on Lovcen
description: Four hundred and sixty-one steps through a mountain tunnel to a black granite mausoleum at 1,660 metres, with the best panorama of the Bay of Kotor anywhere in the country.

title: Walk the old royal capital of Cetinje
description: Montenegro's low-key former capital, with former foreign embassies from when it was a kingdom now serving as museums. Quieter and cheaper than the coast, twenty minutes above Kotor by road.

title: Swim off Mogren beach below Budva's walls
description: A fortified Venetian old town with a beach on each side, connected by a cliff path. Mogren I gets crowded fast in summer; a short scramble further gets you to the quieter second cove.

title: Walk among the old growth at Biogradska Gora
description: One of Europe's last three primeval forests, with beech and spruce over 500 years old around a still glacial lake. Rowboats are for hire on the lake itself.

title: Hike into the Accursed Mountains from Plav
description: Jagged limestone peaks along the Albanian border, still one of the least-visited ranges in Europe. Trails link up with Albania's Valbona side for anyone doing the multi-day Peaks of the Balkans route.

title: Swim between the islets at Ksamil
description: Four tiny islands close enough to swim or wade to, in water the colour of the Maldives at a fraction of the price. Sunbeds vanish under Italian and Balkan tour groups by 10am in August; go early.

title: Walk the ruins of Butrint
description: Greek, Roman, Byzantine and Venetian layers stacked in one archaeological park on a lagoon, with almost no crowd control needed because so few people make the detour south of Saranda.

title: Peer into the Blue Eye spring
description: A karst spring pushing up cold water from a hole divers have measured past 50 metres without finding the bottom. Swimming is banned at the eye itself, but the river below it is open.

title: Hike the pass from Valbona to Theth
description: A six to eight hour crossing over the Valbona Pass at 1,800 metres through the Accursed Mountains, between two valleys that only connected to the road network this century. Guesthouses at both ends will move your bag for you.

title: Go underground at Bunk'Art
description: A five-storey nuclear bunker built for dictator Enver Hoxha's inner circle, one of over 170,000 bunkers he had built across a country of three million people. Now a museum on the paranoia that built them.

title: Cross Skanderbeg Square at golden hour
description: A vast pedestrian square rebuilt from a communist-era roundabout, ringed by the Et'hem Bey Mosque, the National History Museum's giant mosaic, and pastel Italian-built ministries.

title: Watch the sunset from Lekuresi Castle
description: An Ottoman hilltop fort above Saranda with a restaurant terrace looking across the strait to Corfu, close enough to see cars on the Greek coast road on a clear evening.

title: Walk the ruins of ancient Apollonia
description: A Greek colony that once had a philosophy school Augustus studied at, spread across hills with almost no other visitors. The monastery museum at the site's edge has the best of what was dug up.

title: Climb Rozafa Castle above Shkoder
description: A hilltop fortress above three rivers and a lake, with a foundation legend of a woman walled in alive to make the walls stand. Views reach into Montenegro on a clear day.

title: Float through the Osumi canyon
description: A narrow gorge cut through white rock an hour from Berat, run on small rubber dinghies since it's too shallow and technical for standard rafts. Almost unknown outside Albania until a few years ago.

title: See the church of Sveti Jovan at Kaneo
description: A 13th-century chapel on a cliff edge above the lake, painted on more Macedonian postcards than any other single building. Come near sunset when the tour buses have gone.

title: Walk the walls of Samuel's Fortress
description: A medieval Bulgarian tsar's stronghold above the old town, with ramparts you can walk the full circuit of for a view over both the lake and the terracotta roofs below.

title: Cross the Stone Bridge into the Old Bazaar
description: The Ottoman-era bazaar on the north bank, the largest outside Istanbul, sitting in contrast to the neoclassical statues and facades the government built across the river after 2010.

title: Ride the cable car up to the Millennium Cross
description: One of the tallest crosses in the world, on Mount Vodno above the city, lit up at night and visible from most of Skopje. The cable car up is faster than the hiking trail and runs most of the year.

title: Hike or ski Mavrovo National Park
description: North Macedonia's largest national park, with a lake, a ski resort, and one of the last wolf and bear populations in the southern Balkans. The submerged church tower of Sveti Nikola breaks the lake surface when levels drop.

title: Stand at the Kokino megalithic observatory
description: A Bronze Age astronomical site on a hilltop, ranked by NASA among the oldest solar observatories in the world. Markers on the rock align with sunrise on the solstices, and almost nobody visits to see it.

title: Taste Vranec at a Tikves winery
description: The Balkans' biggest wine region, producing the dark, tannic Vranec grape found on most Macedonian restaurant lists. Tastings at the larger estates are easy to arrange without a tour.

title: Wade the fifth season floods at Soomaa
description: Snowshoe-like bog shoes let you walk on ground that would otherwise swallow a boot, over pools 10,000 years in the making. Every spring the rivers flood the forest into a fifth season, when locals swap the shoes for canoes.

title: Wander the wooden streets of Kalamaja
description: A former fishermen's and factory-workers' district of wooden houses, now cafes and studios around the old Soviet submarine hall at Seaplane Harbour. Ten minutes' walk from the medieval old town, but nothing like it.

title: Spend a summer afternoon on Parnu beach
description: Estonia's self-declared summer capital, a white sand beach backed by pine trees and Soviet-era sanatoriums since rebuilt as spas. The water is shallow enough to wade out a long way.

title: Explore Estonia's university town of Tartu
description: Home to the country's oldest university since 1632, with a leaning bridge, a hilltop park of ruined cathedral walls, and a student culture that keeps the whole town young.

title: Cross the moat into Kuressaare's bishop's castle
description: The best-preserved medieval castle in the Baltics, a stone fortress with an intact moat on Estonia's largest island. Saaremaa spent centuries answering to Danish, Swedish, German and Russian rulers in turn, and the castle shows every layer.

title: Watch seals off Vilsandi National Park
description: Estonia's oldest protected area, a scatter of over a hundred islets off Saaremaa where grey seals haul out and migrating birds stop by the thousand. Boat trips leave from the western coast when the sea allows.

title: Climb St Peter's tower over Riga's old town
description: A UNESCO old town of guild halls and the House of the Blackheads, rebuilt after wartime bombing from old photographs. The lift up St Peter's spire gives the view the ground-level streets can't.

title: Walk the grounds of Turaida Castle
description: A rebuilt medieval red-brick castle in Gauja National Park, with a folk song hill and the grave of the 'Rose of Turaida' below it. Pair it with Gutmanis Cave, the biggest grotto in the Baltics, a short walk down the valley.

title: Tour the state rooms of Rundale Palace
description: A Baroque summer palace by the architect of St Petersburg's Winter Palace, built for a Duke of Courland and restored room by room since Soviet times. The French formal gardens behind it are worth the extra ticket.

title: Walk the beach promenade at Jurmala
description: Thirty kilometres of white sand backed by wooden Tsarist-era holiday villas, twenty minutes from Riga by train. A Soviet-era spa culture survives in the sanatoriums that still line the dunes.

title: Ride the Sigulda Olympic bobsled track
description: A real World Cup bobsled and luge track built in 1986, open to the public in a wheeled summer cart or a winter sled with a professional driver. Hits speeds of 80 km/h in under a minute.

title: Visit the Aglona Basilica on assumption day
description: The Baltics' biggest Catholic pilgrimage site, drawing over a hundred thousand people every August 15th to a basilica between two lakes in Latvia's most Polish-influenced region.

title: Cross the footbridge to Trakai island castle
description: A red-brick castle rebuilt on its own island in a lake chain, once the capital of a Grand Duchy that stretched to the Black Sea. Rent a kayak instead of just the footbridge and circle it from the water.

title: Ride the funicular up Gediminas' Tower
description: The last remnant of Vilnius' upper castle, on the hill where the city's founding is said to have been dreamed by a duke. Independence rallies gathered here in 1991 while Soviet tanks were still in the streets.

title: Walk the cells of the Vilnius KGB museum
description: Interrogation rooms and a padded execution chamber, preserved in the basement of the former KGB headquarters. Used continuously as a prison from 1940 until 1991, under three different occupying regimes.

title: Walk the pier at Palanga at sunset
description: Lithuania's biggest beach resort, with a wooden sea bridge built for sunset walks and an amber museum inside a count's old palace and rose garden.

title: Walk among the toppled statues at Grutas Park
description: Lenin, Stalin and dozens of other Soviet statues pulled off their pedestals after 1990 and gathered in a forest park, half museum and half theme park - it was pitched to a TV network as 'Stalin World' before opening.

title: Canoe the lakes of Aukstaitija
description: Lithuania's oldest national park, a hundred and twenty-six lakes linked by pine forest, best seen from a multi-day canoe route between villages that still smoke fish over alder wood.

title: Tour the fairytale rooms of Bojnice Castle
description: Slovakia's most visited castle, remodelled in the 1900s into a French-chateau fantasy by the industrialist who owned it. An international ghost festival takes over the halls every May.

title: Stand at the ruins of Devin Castle
description: A ruined clifftop fortress where the Morava river joins the Danube and the Iron Curtain once ran straight through the water. A short bus ride from central Bratislava.

title: Walk the ice formations of Demanovska cave
description: One of the few caves in Europe with ice that survives into summer, in a valley of the Low Tatras riddled with over forty kilometres of passages. Bring a jacket regardless of the weather outside.

title: See the painted houses of Cicmany
description: Log houses lime-washed white and hand-painted with lace-like geometric patterns, a tradition that started after a fire in 1921 and became the village's trademark. One of the first folk sites protected in Europe.

title: Climb the cliffside rooms of Orava Castle
description: A castle built up a rock outcrop in stages over five centuries, used as Count Orlok's home in the 1922 film Nosferatu. The uppermost tower is a genuine climb, not just a walk.

title: Walk the mining town of Banska Stiavnica
description: A silver and gold mining town that funded the Habsburg empire and hosted the world's first mining academy, now a hillside of baroque houses over flooded pit lakes called tajchy.

title: Hike the ridgeline above Vratna valley
description: A cable car up Snilovske sedlo saves half the climb to the ridge of the Mala Fatra, in the valley where the folk-hero outlaw Juraj Janosik is said to have hidden. Limestone crags called Tiesnavy pinch the trail to a rope-assisted scramble lower down.

title: Watch the singing fountain in Kosice's old town
description: Slovakia's second city and a former European Capital of Culture, built around the largest Gothic cathedral in the country. The fountain in the main square runs a light-and-music show most summer evenings.

title: Take a boat through the Blue Grotto sea caves
description: Traditional luzzu boats duck through a string of sea caves lit an electric blue by refracted sunlight. Go before 10am - the boats stop running in rough seas and the light is best in the morning.

title: Stand inside temples older than the pyramids
description: Two megalithic temple complexes on a clifftop, built from limestone slabs around 3600 BC - older than Stonehenge or the Giza pyramids. Tent-like canopies now protect the stone from the same weather that has eroded it for 5,000 years.

title: Watch the sunset from Gozo's Citadel
description: A walled hilltop fortress over Victoria that held the entire island's population during pirate raids, when residents had to sleep inside every night for safety. The restored ramparts give a 360-degree view of Gozo's whole coastline.

title: Swim in Comino's Blue Lagoon
description: Shallow turquoise water over white sand between Comino and a tiny islet, with almost no permanent population to share it with - except the day-tripper boats that fill it by 11am. An early or late ferry beats the crowd.

title: Wander the film set at Popeye Village
description: A wooden fishing village built for the 1980 Robin Williams film Popeye and kept standing ever since as a waterfront park. Sits on a genuinely striking bay, film set or not.

title: See the oldest free-standing structures on earth at Ggantija
description: Two temples on Gozo dated to around 3600 BC, predating the pyramids by a thousand years. Local legend credited them to a giantess who carried the stones on her head, which is roughly how heavy they look.

title: Browse the Sunday fish market at Marsaxlokk
description: A working fishing harbour of orange, yellow and blue luzzu boats, each painted with a pair of eyes on the bow to ward off misfortune. Sunday brings a market of fish, produce and tourist stalls along the whole waterfront.

title: Watch a play in the Greco-Roman theatre at Kourion
description: A cliff-edge theatre with the Mediterranean as its backdrop, still hosting performances in summer nearly two thousand years after it was built. The mosaic floors of the House of Eustolios, just below it, survived an earthquake that levelled most of the city in 365 AD.

title: Find the frescoes hidden in the Troodos painted churches
description: Ten Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches scattered through mountain villages, plain steep-roofed shells outside and wall-to-wall fresco inside. Most keep a caretaker's phone number pinned to the door rather than fixed opening hours.

title: Walk the underground Tombs of the Kings at Paphos
description: Rock-cut tombs from the 4th century BC carved to imitate the houses of the living, despite the name built for aristocrats rather than royalty. There's almost no shade, so a morning visit beats the afternoon sun.

title: Watch the sunset at Aphrodite's Rock
description: A sea stack off the coast road where legend says Aphrodite rose from the foam, with a pebble beach opposite for the view rather than easy swimming. Sunset lines the rock up with the road behind it, and the car park empties out fast after.

title: Walk the Green Line through central Nicosia
description: A UN-patrolled buffer zone has run through the last divided capital in Europe since 1974, and the Ledra Street crossing lets you walk from one side to the other on foot with a passport. Bring ID - the checkpoint is a working border post, not a photo opportunity.

title: See the mosaic floors of the House of Dionysus
description: Roman villa floors depicting the god Dionysus and scenes from Greek myth, preserved almost intact under later layers of soil until a farmer's plough struck them in 1962. Raised walkways cover most of the site so nothing underfoot is missed.

title: Walk the Neolithic village of Choirokoitia
description: Circular stone houses from one of the best-preserved Neolithic settlements in the eastern Mediterranean, inhabited from around 7000 BC. A handful have been rebuilt full-height to show how they actually looked.

title: Visit the gilded interior of Kykkos Monastery
description: Cyprus' wealthiest and most important monastery, its courtyards covered floor to ceiling in gold-backed mosaics telling its own founding story. It holds an icon of the Virgin Mary so sacred it stays permanently covered from view.

title: Watch the flamingos on Larnaca Salt Lake
description: Thousands of migrating flamingos winter on a lake bed that dries into a walkable salt crust by summer. The 16th-century Hala Sultan Tekke mosque sits right on its edge, one of Islam's most important pilgrimage sites outside the Middle East's main countries.

title: Hike the sea caves of Cape Greco
description: Cliff paths link natural arches, sea caves and a submerged sculpture park you can snorkel straight out to from the rocks. Far less built-up than the Ayia Napa strip it borders.

title: Explore Kyrenia's Venetian harbour castle
description: A Byzantine, then Venetian, fortress guarding a horseshoe harbour on the island's north coast, home to the wreck of a 4th-century BC Greek merchant ship raised nearly whole. This side of the island has used a different currency and administration since 1974, so check current entry requirements before planning a crossing.

title: Climb the Crusader keep at Kolossi Castle
description: A squat stone keep built by the Knights Hospitaller, who ran a sugar plantation and refinery here that once supplied crusader Europe. The roof gives a flat view over the vineyards that grow the local Commandaria dessert wine.

title: Hike the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley
description: Andorra's only UNESCO World Heritage site, a glacial valley of stone shepherd huts and terraced fields that shows a thousand years of mountain farming. No road reaches it - every visitor arrives on foot.

title: Tour Andorra's old parliament at Casa de la Vall
description: A 16th-century stone manor that served as the seat of Andorra's government until 2011, with a council chamber that still locks its decisions in a cabinet with six keys, one per parish.

title: Ski Grandvalira, the Pyrenees' biggest resort
description: Over 200 kilometres of linked pistes across two valleys, built up because skiing and duty-free shopping are most of what keeps Andorra's economy running. Lift lines are shortest on weekday mornings outside French and Spanish school holidays.

title: Visit the sanctuary of Andorra's patron saint
description: A modernist basilica rebuilt after a 1972 fire destroyed the original chapel, holding the statue of the Virgin of Meritxell that Andorrans credit with the country's protection. September 8th is a national holiday built entirely around it.

title: Look inside the Belle Epoque halls of the Monte Carlo Casino
description: Gilded gaming rooms that funded the principality when Monaco abolished taxes for its own citizens in the 1860s. A general admission ticket gets you into the ornate public rooms even if you don't gamble.

title: Watch the changing of the guard at the Prince's Palace
description: An 11:55am ceremony outside the ruling Grimaldi family's home, on a clifftop rock the family has held since 1297 - Europe's longest-ruling dynasty. The palace's state rooms open to the public only when the Prince isn't in residence.

title: Climb into the cave below the Jardin Exotique
description: Thousands of cacti and succulents planted down a cliff face, above a limestone cave with stalactites reaching almost to the sea. The steep paths aren't stroller or wheelchair friendly - the drop is the whole point of the view.

title: Walk the superyacht docks of Port Hercules
description: The floating heart of the Grand Prix track and the Monaco Yacht Show, lined with vessels that can cost more than the apartments overlooking them. Free to walk, and free to feel underdressed.

title: Climb the second tower, Cesta, for the arms museum
description: The tallest of San Marino's three fortresses, now a museum of medieval and Renaissance weapons, reached by the ridge path from Guaita. Wind on the exposed walkway between the towers can be sharp even in summer.

title: See the private third tower, Montale, from the ridge trail
description: Never open to the public and rarely photographed as well as its two neighbours because fewer people walk this far along the ridge. The path here thins out and the crowds mostly stop at Cesta.

title: Watch the guard change in Piazza della Liberta
description: The ceremonial heart of the world's oldest republic, in front of a government palace still in active use. The guard change happens on the hour and draws a bigger crowd than its five-minute length suggests.

title: Ride the cable car down to Borgo Maggiore market
description: San Marino's real working town, below the tourist-facing City on the peak, with a Thursday market that's sold produce since the 1600s. The cable car ride down is worth doing for its own sake.

title: Photograph Vaduz Castle from the vineyard path
description: The reigning prince's actual home, on a wooded outcrop above the capital, and closed to the public because of it. A marked path through the vineyards below gives the best photo without trespassing on the family's front lawn.

title: Walk a stage of the Liechtenstein Trail
description: A 75-kilometre route opened in 2019 that strings together all eleven municipalities, walkable end to end in about five days or sampled in single afternoon stages by bus back to Vaduz.

title: Browse Vaduz's stamp and art museums
description: A capital small enough to see on foot in an afternoon, with a postage stamp museum that explains how stamp sales alone used to fund a meaningful share of the state budget.

title: Ski Liechtenstein's only resort at Malbun
description: A small, unglamorous resort at the end of a dead-end mountain road, with beginner-friendly slopes and none of the prices or crowds of its Austrian and Swiss neighbours.

title: Visit the cave monastery at Orheiul Vechi
description: A monastery carved into a limestone cliff above the Raut river, still used by a handful of monks, on a site occupied on and off since the Stone Age. The village of Butuceni below keeps traditional Moldovan houses along a single dirt lane.

title: Drive the wine cellars of Cricova
description: Over a hundred kilometres of former limestone quarry turned wine cellar, toured by golf cart because walking it all isn't practical. Heads of state and half of Europe's political class have wine bottled here under their own names.

title: Tour the world's largest wine collection at Milestii Mici
description: A Guinness World Record two million bottles held in underground streets long enough to need street names and traffic signs. Some of the reserve wines here predate Moldovan independence.

title: Walk the boulevards of Chisinau
description: Europe's least-visited capital, rebuilt in wide Soviet boulevards after the Second World War, with a triumphal arch, a yellow-stone cathedral, and a park culture that fills every bench on a warm evening.

title: Cross into Transnistria to see Tiraspol
description: A breakaway strip along the Ukrainian border that still flies a hammer-and-sickle flag and uses its own currency, unrecognised by any UN member including Moldova itself. Crossing is currently straightforward for most nationalities at the checkpoint, but confirm the latest advice before going - the region sits close to the war in Ukraine.

title: Taste Negru de Purcari at Chateau Purcari
description: A winery founded in 1827 whose Negru de Purcari red was reportedly a favourite of the British royal family, on the Dniester near the Ukrainian border. The estate's own microclimate is credited for grapes ripening further north than they should.

title: See the Byzantine mosaics of Saint Sophia Cathedral
description: An 11th-century cathedral with its original mosaics and frescoes largely intact, one of the few Kyivan Rus buildings to survive Mongol invasion, Soviet demolition plans and, so far, the current war. Ukraine is under an active do-not-travel advisory; this is a record of what the country holds, not a current itinerary.

title: Walk the underground caves of the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
description: A monastery complex of gold domes above catacombs where mummified monks have lain in glass cases for centuries, candle in hand as you file past in the dark. Founded in 1051 and still an active monastery between the museum sections.

title: Wander the UNESCO old town of Lviv
description: A central European old town of Austro-Hungarian, Polish and Ukrainian layers that came through the Second World War largely undamaged, unlike almost every other major Ukrainian city. The furthest west and generally calmest part of the country, though still under wartime air alerts.

title: Walk the abandoned streets of Pripyat in the Chernobyl zone
description: Guided day trips from Kyiv ran routinely to the reactor and the ghost city of Pripyat until Russian forces occupied and dug trenches in the radioactive Red Forest in early 2022. Tours have not consistently resumed since; check current status before planning anything.

title: Cross the canyon bridge to Kamianets-Podilskyi fortress
description: An Old Town fortress that sits on an island formed by a river canyon looping almost back on itself, crossed by a single bridge. Rated among the most dramatic castle settings in Europe, and far enough from the front line to have stayed largely untouched by the war so far.

title: Walk down the Potemkin Stairs in Odesa
description: One hundred and ninety-two steps down to the Black Sea harbour, made famous by Eisenstein's 1925 film Battleship Potemkin. Odesa's historic centre earned UNESCO listing in 2023, the same year Russian strikes damaged part of it - a status meant to draw protection as much as visitors.

title: Hike to the summit of Hoverla, Ukraine's highest peak
description: A 2,061-metre summit in the Hutsul highlands, normally a straightforward day hike from Ukraine's most peaceful region. Trailhead access has varied through the war; local guides are the most reliable source on current conditions.

title: Stand in Maidan Nezalezhnosti, Independence Square
description: The square at the centre of two revolutions, in 2004 and 2014, now lined with flags planted for every soldier killed since 2022. Less a tourist sight than a place to understand what the country is currently living through.

title: Cross the moat into Mir Castle
description: A red-brick Gothic-Renaissance castle rebuilt from ruin across three centuries, UNESCO listed for the sheer range of architectural styles stitched into one building. Belarus currently carries a do-not-travel advisory for foreign nationals over detention risk; this is a record of the country's heritage, not a current recommendation.

title: Tour the Radziwill family seat at Nesvizh
description: A moated palace that housed one of Eastern Europe's most powerful noble families for four centuries, with a landscaped park and a chain of ponds dug by hand. Paired with Mir Castle on the same UNESCO listing, 100 kilometres apart.

title: Look for European bison in the Bialowieza Forest
description: The last major remnant of the primeval forest that once covered the European plain, and home to the continent's largest land animal, the European bison, reintroduced here after it went extinct in the wild. The forest straddles the Polish border; the two sides are separately managed and not connected without a formal crossing.

title: See the diamond-shaped National Library of Belarus
description: A capital almost entirely rebuilt in wide Stalinist boulevards after 1944, with a 2006 library shaped like a giant illuminated rhombicuboctahedron on its edge. Foreign nationals currently face real detention risk in Belarus; treat this as background on the country, not travel advice.

title: Stand in Red Square between the Kremlin and GUM
description: Cobblestones between the Kremlin wall, Lenin's mausoleum and a 19th-century department store now selling Western luxury brands under sanctions-era workarounds. Russia currently carries a do-not-travel advisory over the war, sanctions and closed airspace to most of the world; this reflects the country's landmarks, not present-day advice to go.

title: Walk the maze of chapels inside St Basil's Cathedral
description: Nine separate chapels under those onion domes, each a distinct, low-ceilinged space rather than one grand nave. Legend holds Ivan the Terrible blinded the architect afterward so he could never build anything to rival it - almost certainly untrue, but it's the story every guide tells.

title: Tour the armoury and cathedrals inside the Kremlin walls
description: A walled complex of onion-domed cathedrals and the tsars' treasury, still the working seat of the Russian government behind its public-facing half. The Armoury's ticket allocation sells out by mid-morning on a normal day.

title: Get lost in the Hermitage's three million objects
description: The Winter Palace of the tsars turned into one of the largest art museums on earth - walking every gallery for a minute each would take over a week. Western credit cards no longer work anywhere in the country, so budget cash brought in advance.

title: Ride a stretch of the Trans-Siberian Railway
description: Nine thousand two hundred and eighty-nine kilometres of track from Moscow to Vladivostok, the longest railway line in the world, crossing eight time zones over about a week end to end. Almost no direct flights connect Russia to Western Europe or North America now, so getting to the start line is its own undertaking.

title: Swim or dive in Lake Baikal
description: The deepest and oldest lake on the planet, holding roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water, so clear you can see twenty metres down from a boat. In winter the surface freezes into clear ice slabs people drive cars across.

title: See the all-wood church built without a single nail at Kizhi
description: A 22-dome wooden church built in 1714 using nothing but axes, notched logs and wooden pegs - no nails anywhere in the structure. Reachable only by boat, on an island that also holds a working open-air museum of relocated peasant houses and windmills.

title: Hike an active volcano in Kamchatka
description: Twenty-nine active volcanoes on a peninsula with no roads connecting it to the rest of Russia - every trip starts with a flight into Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky. Helicopter transfers to the more remote craters are standard, since most of the terrain has no trails at all.

title: Watch the fountains start at Peterhof without a single pump
description: Peter the Great's answer to Versailles, its 150-plus fountains run entirely on gravity from elevated springs, with no mechanical pumps at all since the 18th century. The Grand Cascade below the palace is switched on each morning to a recorded fanfare.

title: Cycle between the monasteries of Suzdal
description: A Golden Ring town frozen at village scale, with more churches and monasteries than modern buildings and no high-rises breaking the skyline of onion domes. Small enough to see entirely by rented bike in a day.

title: Climb to the Motherland Calls statue at Mamayev Kurgan
description: An 85-metre sword-wielding statue over the mass graves of the Battle of Stalingrad, once the tallest statue in the world, on a hill where the fighting was so intense that unexploded ordnance is still found in the ground each year.

title: See the mosque and cathedral share a skyline at the Kazan Kremlin
description: A walled citadel where the blue-domed Qol Sharif Mosque and the Orthodox Annunciation Cathedral stand a few hundred metres apart, reflecting Tatarstan's mixed Muslim-Christian history. Kazan itself keeps a distinct Tatar language and identity within Russia.
